data.name: Edy
data.gender_notes: Edy is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name 'Hadē', meaning 'sea' or 'wealth'. In Greek mythology, Hadē was the goddess of the sea and the wife of Poseidon. This name is also associated with prosperity and abundance. The name Edy carries the meaning “Wealth, Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Edy usually hope their child will grow to embody wealth, prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the abundance of God's blessings in one's life.
data.etymology: Edy belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wealth, Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Edy total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_greek.name: Έντυ
in_greek.meaning: Το Έντυ σημαίνει πλούσιο δώρο ή επίγειος πλούτος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Έντυ προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'Ευδокиμία' που σημαίνει πλούσιο δώρο ή επίγειος πλούτος. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα αυτό συμβολίζει τη γενναιοδωρία και την πλούσια χάρη του Θεού.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Edy" holds cultural significance in its Greek origins, with connections to the Greek goddess Hadē, whom the name is derived from. Hadē was revered in Greek culture as the goddess of the sea, symbolizing the vast, powerful, and life-giving body of water. For those of Greek descent, the name "Edy" may carry connotations of this ancient tradition and cultural heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Edy" may have spiritual significance rooted in its ancient Greek background as the name of a goddess associated with prosperity, wealth, and abundance. It may inspire those who bear the name to reflect on the spiritual values of these concepts and how they can be cultivated and expressed in their own lives. Additionally, the name may serve as a reminder of the interconnectedness and abundance of God's creation, particularly the vast and profound beauty of the sea.
